feature: Board layout: question, option columns, wires
description: Dark question box above 2–4 dark option headers, columns of argument rows connected by wires; per-space canvas behind.
tier_why: The shared surface where a group builds the steelman.
complexity_why: Wires, column widths and horizontal row scroll need careful layout code; can largely port from prototype.
design_gaps: In the app (Nov 22): the prototype's wires from the question to each option header and down each column to every row, following unfolding, marked rows, options, History, Strongest case, and the phone layout. Polished. Phone layout of wide boards still cramped. Since Nov 17, the importance axis shows only once some column has two arguments to rank (on a phone, per column). Since M3d-10 (Nov 25), while the board's first read is on its way, skeleton cards stand in the board's own layout (the dark question, two option headers, and cards under each; on a phone, one column under the strip of sides) with the status "The steelman is loading." The status region is on the page before its sentence arrives, and only the hidden blocks are marked busy. They fade in after twice --sm-slow, as GitHub's Primer shows nothing for a quick load, pulse gently, and stay still under reduced motion. An Owner's or Editor's board also has the column to add an option, which the skeleton, drawn before the role is known, leaves out. Nov 26 (M3d-21): the board's canvas has index and fine contours and is lit from the top centre, under the question, and so is its skeleton. Nov 26 (M3d-22): the board's tint, contours, and grain are drawn again on a layer of its own, in a frame that shares the surface's one grid cell with the scene, and they drift down a tenth as far as the page scrolls once the board's top has left the window, up to 170 px. The light holds still above them. The frame clips the layer, so the scroll height and the cards' click targets are unchanged, and at the top of the page it draws what the surface did, to within one level in 255. The hex texture stays with its columns.

description: Edit wording and context in place, any time (like Reddit); the byline says 'edited', which shows the earlier wording. Importance and articulation votes stay; credibility assessments start over, with a warning before saving. Delete with Undo.
tier_why: Not needed for the loop (a better version can replace it), but people must be able to fix or retract their own mistakes before real use.
complexity_why: Revision history per version; resetting assessments while keeping votes.
design_gaps: In the app (M1-10): edited in place from the ⋯ menu, with "The credibility score resets when you save." once the text changes on an assessed wording; deleted with a ten-second Undo held in the browser, sent at once if the tab closes. Since Nov 18 (M2-5, Q22): hovering 'edited' (tapping, on a phone) also shows, under the earlier wording, how many importance and articulation votes it had just before the latest edit, as saved with that revision; later votes don't change it. Full revision history beyond the previous wording not designed. Since Nov 25 (M3d-4): your deleted version leaves through a copy of its card that screen readers and the cursor skip: its wording fades and its height eases into the dashed placeholder, and then it fades and leaves. The board takes its layout without the card at once, as before, so the rows below take their places at once and nothing animates on them. The plan row's wording that the rows below close the gap only on Update conflicts with the rule that every animation ends in today's layout, and awaits the builder. Since M3d-6 (Nov 25), an edit in progress in a column the reader hides closes and keeps its text, and Edit on that wording again opens it as the reader left it; Cancel and Save still end it, and switching to Strongest case still discards it.

description: Drag merge icon onto another argument (or click to pick); drop on Add an argument slot to separate; votes and comments travel; 10-second Undo.
tier_why: Duplicates appear as soon as several people write, splitting importance votes. First enhancement; the PRD's trial rules expect it.
complexity_why: PRD vote-merge rules (dedupe per participant, conflicting votes pending), identity redirects, reversible history.
design_gaps: Nov 22: the dialog says in one light gray line what happens to the votes. Designed in the prototype (M3a-5, Nov 22, revised at the builder's direction): a drag or "Combine here" moves the one wording dragged, with its votes, assessments, and comments; the two arguments become one only when it was its argument's last wording, and then importance votes merge per person. A short dialog confirms first (the question, the wordings, Cancel and Combine or Separate), saying only who must vote again. A "vote again" note marks the combined argument for someone whose two votes disagreed. On the service (M3a-6): combine, separate, and undo, with votes kept for undo in combine_vote. On the board (M3a-7): the merge handle's drag and press, the menu's Combine and Separate, the dialog, ten seconds of Undo, the vote-again note, and the combined-away row for other readers. Undo from History: M3a-8. Audited Nov 22: the menu reads Combine… and Separate…; "Combine here" leaves the wording readable; "Vote again" is a chip with the vote ringed; an undo never leaves an argument empty. The builder, Nov 22: a vote queued for an argument combined away replaces the vote the combine carried over, when the person cast none there themselves. Since Nov 25 (M3d-7): a combine or a separation settles in place. A wording combined away into a row already drawn fades out where it was on an inert copy of its card, drawn over what took its place, at --sm-medium; a separated wording leaves no copy, and its new row rises 8 px and fades in at its place in the same column; each stack whose count changed settles with one scale on --sm-settle. The rows below take their places at once, as before, because cards move only on Update (question 7). No card crosses rows or columns, and the dialog and its sentences are unchanged.

description: Order set by shared votes, never by your own, and fixed when the board opens. A pill counts changes from others ('3 changes · Update'); Update or reload applies them, holding the row you're reading in place, and Update slides the rows that moved into the new order.
tier_why: Votes must produce a shared order for the strongest case to surface. Stable layout keeps collaborators from losing their place; explicit apply could start simpler.
complexity_why: Aggregation, batching/ticks, pushing 'new order available' to open clients without moving layout.
design_gaps: None at design level: the shared order recalculates on a per-board tick (60 s for the class trial), lazily on the next request (plans/architecture.md §3). Update moves the rows into the new order (M3d-3, Nov 25): each row that moved slides from where it was on --sm-slow and --sm-settle, wearing --sm-lift and growing to 1.01 while it travels, a row moving up passes over a row moving down, and the row being read stays still. Under reduced motion the rows take their places at once. On a short page, the page can't scroll far enough to hold the row being read when rows move above it, with motion or without.

description: A link (http or https), a title, and an optional description; who added it ('You' for your own); the prototype's free-text 'where to find it' and optional Backs up & Limits dropped (the builder, Nov 14–15); Undo.
tier_why: Credibility judgments need inspectable evidence.
design_gaps: Built on the server (M1-8) and on the card (M1-9); the first example board carries the prototype's sources. Reworked with the builder (Nov 14–15), after Google Docs' Insert link and Wikipedia's citation tool: the form asks for a Link first (with a link icon; http or https only, up to 2,000 characters, since there are no uploads yet), then a Title, then an optional Description, each with an example; Backs up and Limits dropped (the description can say them), and who added a source is shown instead; the columns stay. Reset warnings say the credibility score resets. As in the prototype, anyone who can contribute adds a source to a wording; only the person who added it edits it. Taking a source off a wording is for whoever added it, the wording's author, or the Owner (the builder, Nov 14; the Editor takes the Owner's place when M2 adds it). One source can back several wordings: a source already on the board can be cited on another. Taking a source off a wording leaves it on the board, since nothing is removed from a board. Remove takes it off at once with a ten-second Undo, held in the browser as a deleted wording is, in place of the prototype's second click (the builder, Nov 15). Where to find it stays text, and is a link only when it is an http or https address. Not designed: a way to pick a source already on the board, which the prototype doesn't have.

description: Speech bubble on question, option, and version with counts; side panel; reply, resolve/reopen, delete own; ⌘/Ctrl+Enter.
tier_why: Discussion supports collaboration, but the steelman is built through arguments, versions, and votes.
design_gaps: In the app since M3b-8 and M3b-9 (Nov 24): the service keeps comments. Anyone who can read adds one on the question, an option, or a wording, on a closed board too, up to 1,000 characters with line breaks kept; only its author deletes it, which erases the text and keeps the row. Anyone who can read also replies to a thread, one level deep, and resolves or reopens any thread, which sets a flag on its first comment. A reply to a reply, to a resolved thread, or naming another target than its thread's is refused. A thread whose first comment its author deleted or a moderator hid takes no reply, resolve, or reopen, as in the prototype. Comments and replies count against a limit of their own, 60 an hour per account; resolving, reopening, and deleting aren't counted. A comment follows its wording through combine and separate. Deleting an account erases its comments' text and author, and Download your data lists them. Since M3b-10, comments reach every reader in the snapshot and in each poll's changes, and a deleted comment arrives with no text. A comment on a deleted or hidden wording or on a deleted option isn't sent, and History's Restore sends the subject's comments again. Helpers in shared/ give a target's threads and the number for its speech bubble, as the prototype counts it. Since M3b-11 (Nov 24), the board shows them: the prototype's speech bubble with its count on each card (between the merge handle and the sources, with a class of its own), on each option's header for every role, and in the question's header, named "3 comments on this version" or "Comment on this option", drawn at full strength. It opens Comments in the drawer History and Settings use, now fixed to the window at every width and covering the board at 640 px and narrower. The panel quotes its subject (Question, Option, or Version) and rings it on the board, lists the open threads with their replies, each with the author's initials and username ("You" for yours) and a time with the full date behind it, says "There are no comments yet." when there are none, and ends with the box "Add a comment" and Comment, which ⌘/Ctrl + Enter presses. The comment text, the quote, and the box carry ph-no-capture. Comments are sent at once, not queued: offline, at the limit, and on a wording removed meanwhile, the panel says so and the text stays in the box. A draft is kept for each subject while the board is open. When someone else deletes or hides the open subject, the panel closes on the next poll, and when the reader deletes it, the panel closes at once. A comment shows the line breaks it was written with. Panels fade in and out, and a comment that arrives rises in. Since M3b-12 (Nov 24), each comment carries the prototype's small text buttons in its order: Reply on an open thread's first comment, Resolve or Reopen on the first comment, and Delete on your own, with none on a deleted or hidden comment. Reply opens the prototype's inline form, "Reply" with Cancel and Reply, which ⌘/Ctrl + Enter presses; Escape closes the reply before the panel, and an empty reply says "Write a reply first." Resolved threads fold under the prototype's "1 resolved" toggle and leave the bubble's count, and with every thread resolved the panel says "Every comment here is resolved." Delete asks first, in place, "Delete this comment?" with Delete and Cancel; a first comment with replies stays as "This comment was deleted.", and any other is removed. The status line says "Your reply was added.", "The thread is resolved. It is under Resolved.", "The thread is open again.", and "Your comment was deleted.", and the cursor goes back to Reply or into the comment box. A reply to a thread someone just resolved says "This thread was resolved, so your reply wasn’t added.", and its draft stays beside the thread's Reopen. A thread or a reply that goes folds away, and a reopened thread rises in. A thread with a reply form or Delete's question open stays in place when someone resolves it meanwhile, and when someone else's change takes away the control that had the cursor, the cursor goes into the comment box. A reply that's added while the reader typed more keeps the new text in the box. The reply box and its text carry ph-no-capture. Since M3b-13 (Nov 24), every standing comment, replies and resolved threads included, carries Link between Resolve and Delete, as in the prototype; it copies the comment's address, /b/<board>/c/<comment>, and says "Link copied.", with the cursor kept on Link. A deleted or hidden comment has no Link. A panel opened by a comment's link starts on that comment: resolved threads are unfolded when its thread is resolved, and the comment is scrolled into view, ringed once, and focused, so its name is read. Since M3b-14 (Nov 24), an Editor or the Owner hides someone else's comment, replies included, with one of the report reasons and restores it, with the `hide` action, so neither on a closed board. Hide sits last among the comment's buttons and puts "Hide it as" with Spam, Abusive, Off-topic, Something else, and Cancel in place of them, with the cursor on Cancel; Escape and Cancel put them away and return the cursor to Hide. Everyone else reads "A moderator removed this comment as spam." (or "as abusive.", "as off-topic.", or "A moderator removed this comment.") in its place and is never sent its text, in the snapshot or in changes. Editors and the Owner read the sentence and the text struck through, inside ph-no-capture, with Restore as its only button. The status line says "The comment is hidden." with the cursor on Restore, and "The comment is restored." with the cursor on Hide. Your own comment can't be hidden or restored by you, and a deleted one can't be either. Each is a change row, comment_hidden with its reason and comment_restored, holding no text, and History says who hid or restored "a comment", linking to it so it opens in its panel. A hidden comment's link lands on its sentence. The simulation plays both, with a check that no hidden comment's text reaches anyone but an Editor or the Owner. Not yet: reporting a comment, which needs a table of its own. Since M3d-6 (Nov 25), a link to a comment on an option, or on a wording, in a column the reader hid brings the column back, as a version's link does; the prototype doesn't do this for comments.

description: Shared motion for the app: a settle curve with a small overshoot (about 4 percent) and a lifted shadow as tokens, FLIP moves that end in exactly the final layout, wires that follow moving cards, and one play() that does nothing under reduced motion. Only Update reorders the board; the reader's own add, delete, combine, and separate only animate the layout change the app already makes then. Nothing moves on someone else's vote, and no card crosses rows or columns.
tier_why: The builder asked on Nov 24 for an app that feels designed, with cards that seem to shuffle; the board works without it.
complexity_why: Every animation must end in the final layout, cancel cleanly when changes overlap, keep wires attached, and stop under reduced motion.
design_gaps: Built in M3d-2 (Nov 24): --sm-settle, a linear() spring that overshoots by about 4 percent, and --sm-lift are tokens, and docs/design/README.md describes two curves, the ease and the settle. web/src/board/motion.ts holds play(), which starts nothing under reduced motion, and captureRects() and flip(), which end in exactly the final layout and cancel an earlier move on the same element. With lift, the moving card wears the shadow, and a moving row puts the shadow on its card, never on the whole row. flip() returns { arrivals, animations }, and motion.ts also exports duration() and BOARD_MOVERS. Wires.tsx's redrawWhile() redraws the wires on every frame while cards move and leaves the textures static. The drawer's 160 ms fade, a thread's 220 ms fold, and a link's 1.4 s ring are tokens with the same values. Update is the first caller (M3d-3, Nov 25): it calls flip(before, root, { lift: true, travel: true }). Under travel, a moving row scales to 1.01 halfway as a whole, vote column included, while only its card wears --sm-lift, and a row moving up is raised one z-index for the move only, so it passes over a row moving down. stopMoves() cancels a shuffle still running before a second Update measures, and drawnRect(), which captureRects() and the reading anchor use, measures a row still growing at its own size about its centre, so the second shuffle starts each row where it's seen. Your own add and delete use it next (M3d-4, Nov 25): the new card rises 8 px and fades in at --sm-medium, as the prototype's render(..., 'added') does, and the add slot after it makes room with flip(); a deleted card leaves through an inert copy whose wording fades and whose height eases into the dashed placeholder on --sm-fold, which then fades on --sm-leave and leaves the page; Undo plays it backwards on the card. Only the reader's own additions animate, and under reduced motion there is no copy and nothing plays. Rows unfold and fold, and card details open and close (M3d-5, Nov 25, web/src/board/unfold.ts): Compare eases the board's gridTemplateColumns and the lead card's width on --sm-slow, grows the axis, and slides the versions out from the lead card's x with the prototype's 45 ms stagger, clipped to the right of the lead card; Fold and a closing card's details play on inert copies while the real screen changes at once, and a fold's columns, lead width, and row height wait --sm-medium for the copy to slide home; a second toggle starts every row from where it's drawn mid-motion; only the reader's own toggles animate, and Update stops a toggle still running. Combining and separating use it too (M3d-7, Nov 25, web/src/board/settle.ts): session.ts tells the board as the reader's own combine, separation, or Undo is sent and again just before it shows, and the board then fades a copy of a wording combined away out where it was, settles the changed stacks' counts with one scale on --sm-settle, and rises a new row in; the rows below take their places at once, and Update or a row toggle stops a settle still running. Hiding a column uses it too (M3d-6, Nov 25): the reader's own Hide this column, Show only this column, and a strip's click ease the board's gridTemplateColumns on --sm-slow and --sm-settle through unfold.ts's beforeColumns() and playColumns(), each new strip fades in on --sm-medium, the wires follow, and the same stopRowMotion() cancels it; a link or History showing a hidden column does so at once. Votes use it too (M3d-8, Nov 25, web/src/board/vote-motion.ts): an arrow presses to 0.92 and back at --sm-fast, the number rolls at --sm-medium through an aria-hidden copy of the old figure, clipped to the number's box, while the real number holds the new value from the start, and Update rings the cards someone else added or reworded with a 3 px --sm-ink ring added to the card's shadow (composite add, so a moving card keeps its lift) that fades over 1.6 s, a constant beside --sm-ring's 1.4 s. The views and the list use it too (M3d-9, Nov 25, web/src/board/zoom.ts): the View switch scales the scene from the centred card, a board opened from the list grows out of its post's miniature, and Back shrinks an inert copy of it into the post, each on --sm-slow and --sm-ease with Wires' redrawWhile(), and none plays on a reload or a deep link. The polish pass uses it too (M3d-10, Nov 25): Share, Settings, History, the comments panel, both menus, the problem bar, and the Update pill share one entrance (the prototype's fade and 4 px rise on --sm-medium) and one exit (the same played back on --sm-leave), Share and the menus through drawer.ts's inert copy and the two bars as themselves; a closing drawer's copy no longer jumps with a dashed edge, and every copy keeps the panel's look as it fades; every control on the board, in Share, and in the panels and menus draws one focus ring (2 px solid, ink or white for its ground, 3 px out from a button or link and 1 px out from a field), except a draft card's two fields, which keep the prototype's grey fill, and the New steelman fields, which keep their 3 px ring, both for a later row; and a card lifts 1 px on hover. The pages outside the board use it too (M3d-11, Nov 25): Home, New steelman, Your account, and the privacy page change with the browser's view transition, the new page rising over a picture of the old on --sm-medium while the header stands still, and Back from a board opened from the list, when its post is off screen, fades the board's copy and raises the list; Home shows skeleton posts while it loads; buttons share one press (a 0.97 scale on :active) and one busy state (data-busy, still for twice --sm-slow, then a slow pulse); and Your account's rows rise into place in reading order through play(). M3d-13 and M3d-19 use it next. Question 7 is answered that cards move only on Update, so your own delete's rows below take their places at once, as before, with no motion on them. Nobody has watched the shuffle or the settle curve on a real board yet; the builder watches it on staging. The tier (T3) awaits the builder's agreement under rule 6. The board's canvas drifts as you scroll (M3d-22, Nov 26): motion.ts adds driftOf(), which gives nothing while the board's top is in the window, a tenth of the scroll after that, at most 170 px, and nothing under reduced motion, and startDrift(), one passive scroll listener that writes a single translate3d on the canvas layer per animation frame. The drift isn't a Web Animation, so it doesn't go through play(), and turning reduced motion on puts a drifted canvas back at once. The drift moves in whole device pixels, and while the board itself is animated, as it is while it grows out of its miniature, it waits and is measured again when the animation ends. Going back to the list from a scrolled board, shrinkInto() eases the copy's drifted canvas back to its place on the shrink's duration and curve.
